summary_up_top.suggest: Move the core finding—that water supply makes up 41% of AMRUT projects but 60% of the money while missing spending data—above the site navigation elements.

edits.why: Site navigation and accessibility widgets currently sit above the main lede, burying the hook for mobile readers.
edits.how: Move the title, metadata, and body lede above the 'Skip to article content', 'Text Size', and audio player elements.

edits.why: A massive 11-column table is nearly impossible to read on a mobile phone screen.
edits.how: Convert the 11-column table into a searchable mobile-friendly card list or summary table of top states, linking to the full raw data.

edits.where: What this table can't tell you
edits.why: Paragraph 6 contains 147 words, creating a dense text block that is tiring to scroll through on a phone.
edits.how: Split paragraph 6 into two shorter paragraphs after the sentence discussing Jal Jeevan Mission.

edits.why: Paragraph 9 contains 202 words, which is too long for a single mobile screen block.
edits.how: Break paragraph 9 into three shorter paragraphs at natural topic transitions about data sources and limitations.

edits.why: Placing the massive data table right at the start of the first section overwhelms readers before the argument is established.
edits.how: Move the table further down or place it in an expandable accordion container.

good: Water supply carries the money, not the project count

summary_up_top.suggest: Lead with a concise, phone-friendly hook: *‘AMRUT 2.0’s ₹1.97 lakh crore urban portfolio skews 60% toward water supply—despite being just 41% of projects. Here’s why the data hides critical gaps in spending.’*

edits.why: The H1 is already punchy but could be more mobile-friendly by removing the ₹1.97 lakh crore figure (redundant in the first line) and shortening to: *‘AMRUT 2.0’s Water Supply Bias: 60% of ₹1.97 Lakh Crore Funds Go to 41% of Projects’*
edits.how: Replace H1 with the above, keeping the subheading intact

edits.why: The dense table/charts combo (11 cols × 37 rows + 2 visuals) overwhelms mobile readers. Split into two H2s: one for the text + chart, one for the table.
edits.how: Move the table to a new H2: *‘The breakdown: State-wise projects and costs’* (keep the existing H2 for the text + first chart)

edits.where: H2: Water supply carries the money, not the project count
edits.why: This paragraph introduces a key contrast (cost vs. project count) but lacks visual hierarchy. Add a subheading to signal the shift.
edits.how: Insert before the paragraph: *‘Why water supply dominates the budget (but not the project count)’*

edits.where: para 6 (under H2: What this table can't tell you)
edits.why: The 147-word para mixes two ideas: (1) the table’s limitations vs. (2) the rural JJM comparison. Split to improve scannability.
edits.how: Break into two paras: First para focuses on *‘What the table omits: spending progress, not just approvals’*; second para starts with *‘Unlike Jal Jeevan Mission…’*

edits.why: The boxed note (GB-card) lists 3 fixes but is buried in prose. Convert the key points into a bulleted list for mobile readability.
edits.how: Replace the boxed note with a list titled *‘3 ways to improve transparency’* and pull the 3 bullet points directly from the card’s content

edits.why: The para’s length (202 words) and dense attribution (state-wise data from Ministry) could be split to avoid mobile scroll fatigue.
edits.how: Shorten heading to *‘Data sources and key caveats’* and split the para into two: First para covers *‘All figures sourced from…’*; second para starts with *‘Important limitations…’*

edits.why: The first 400 words include redundant details (e.g., repeating ₹1.97 lakh crore). Trim to focus on the core contrast (41% projects vs. 60% funds).
edits.how: Delete the sentence: *‘Water supply alone is 41% of that project count but 60% of the money…’* (it’s restated in the H1). Start the para with: *‘AMRUT 2.0’s ₹1.97 lakh crore portfolio is skewed: water supply accounts for 60% of funds but just 41% of the 8,777 approved projects. The public data reveals the scale—but not the spending reality.*’

edits.where: table (under H2: Four components, one portfolio)
edits.why: The table’s 11 columns are too wide for mobile. Convert to a stacked table (e.g., 3 columns: *State/UT | Water Supply (₹cr) | Sewerage (₹cr)*) with expandable rows for full data.
edits.how: Use a collapsible table format (e.g., *‘Tap to see full state-wise breakdown’* with a condensed 3-column view by default)
